verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents creating machines through its API and CLI, and it publishes a 61-path OpenAPI spec, a generated REST reference, team-scoped API keys and an official pspace CLI. That covers the provisioning leg of the lifecycle. The pack does not explicitly document the monitoring, workload-execution or teardown/delete steps, and high-end GPUs such as H100 need a human approval request before use. missing for 10: explicit API/CLI docs for monitoring machine state and deleting/tearing down machines, documented programmatic workload execution, approval-free GPU access, any MCP server, independent hands-on corroboration of an end-to-end agent run.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can provision a GPU, monitor it, run a workload, and tear it down end to end through documented APIs, CLI, or MCP without a human in the console

citations.quote: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
Programmatically manage Paperspace resources using conventional HTTP requests.
Programmatically manage resources using the Paperspace Command Line Interface.
The production API domain serves a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0.3 document at /v1/openapi.json
